# Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences (NHESS)

> NHESS is a peer-reviewed open-access journal publishing research on natural hazards, disaster risk reduction, and climate-related Earth system processes.

NHESS is part of the Copernicus Publications portfolio and provides a platform for scientists to share research on topics including rockfall hazards, flooding, landslides, coastal hazards, and multi-hazard risk assessment. The journal operates through a transparent peer-review process and maintains thematic collections on specialized topics like hydrological modeling.

## Journal Navigation

- [Recent Publications](https://nhess.copernicus.org): NHESS homepage showcasing recent publications on natural hazards
- [Journal Volumes](https://nhess.copernicus.org/articles/volumes.html): NHESS journal volumes and article archive index
- [Preprints](https://nhess.copernicus.org/preprints): NHESS preprint archive via EGUsphere for open discussion
- [Collections](https://nhess.copernicus.org/collections.html): Thematic collections including WaterGAP hydrological models

## Featured & Popular Content

- [Editor's Choice](https://nhess.copernicus.org/editors_choice.html): Curated editor selections on hazard assessment and mitigation
- [Most Downloaded](https://nhess.copernicus.org/most_downloaded.html): Popular NHESS articles on flood risk and natural hazards
- [Most Commented](https://nhess.copernicus.org/most_commented.html): Highly discussed NHESS articles on landslides and hazards

## Article Types & Guidelines

- [Research Articles](https://nhess.copernicus.org/research_article.html): Rockfall hazard research article from Skagway, Alaska
- [Review Articles](https://nhess.copernicus.org/review_article.html): Review on natural hazards and disaster management in SE Europe
- [Brief Communications](https://nhess.copernicus.org/brief_communication.html): Brief communication on landslide and climate hazard analysis
- [Invited Perspectives](https://nhess.copernicus.org/invited_perspectives.html): Invited expert perspectives on multi-hazard risk assessment

## Recent Research Highlights

- [Rockfall Hazard Characterization in Skagway, Alaska](https://nhess.copernicus.org/articles/26/1435/2026): Rockfall hazard modeling and inventory study integrating kinematic and runout models
- [Compound Flooding from Tropical Cyclone Idai in Mozambique](https://nhess.copernicus.org/articles/26/1417/2026): Climate attribution of compound flooding from Cyclone Idai
- [ENSO Influence on U.S. Pacific Northwest Coastal Hazards](https://nhess.copernicus.org/articles/26/1397/2026): ENSO teleconnection to coastal hazards in Pacific Northwest
- [Multi-Hazard Risk Assessment in Burundi](https://nhess.copernicus.org/articles/26/1347/2026): Multi-hazard risk assessment methodology for data-scarce regions
- [Landslide Morphology Analysis Using Airborne Laser Scanning](https://nhess.copernicus.org/articles/26/1375/2026): Topographic profile and morphology analysis of shallow landslides with semi-automatic mapping
- [Cloud Seeding for Heavy Rainfall Mitigation in Japan](https://nhess.copernicus.org/articles/26/1287/2026): Numerical experiments of cloud seeding for mitigating localization of heavy rainfall
